# Code of Conduct

Linux System Monitor is an open-source engineering project. Contributors, users and maintainers are expected to keep project spaces professional, constructive and focused on the work.

## Expected conduct

Be respectful of other participants and their time. Discuss technical ideas on their merits. Give actionable feedback, assume good faith where reasonable, and clearly distinguish verified behaviour from hypotheses or untested hardware assumptions.

Harassment, threats, personal attacks, discriminatory abuse, sexual harassment, deliberate disruption, doxxing, or publishing another person's private information without permission are not acceptable.

## Engineering discussions

Disagreement is welcome when it improves the project. Reviews should explain the technical reason for a requested change. Repeatedly derailing discussions, misrepresenting test results, or knowingly presenting guessed hardware behaviour as verified is unacceptable.

Portability, data correctness, privilege boundaries and hardware safety concerns should be raised plainly. No contributor should be pressured to conceal uncertainty or to accept fabricated telemetry merely to make the interface look complete.

## Scope

This code applies to repository issues, pull requests, reviews, discussions, project documentation and other spaces operated for Linux System Monitor. It also applies when someone is representing the project in an official capacity.

## Enforcement

Maintainers may edit or remove inappropriate content, close or lock discussions, reject contributions, or temporarily or permanently restrict participation when necessary to protect the project and its participants.

For conduct concerns that should not be raised publicly, contact the project maintainer privately at `infiltratr@yandex.com`. Reports will be handled as discreetly as reasonably possible.

Enforcement decisions should be proportionate to the behaviour, its impact, any pattern of prior conduct and the need to keep the project safe and productive.
